THE DEAL, THEN THE RESULTS

Trade lab

Who received what—and how much of it reached a starting lineup?

The headline compares received players’ actual starter points during their first stay on each recipient’s roster. It starts the week after the deal and stops at the next exit. Player output includes later production elsewhere. Neither measure estimates replacement players or credits the value of subsequent trades.

Definitions, coverage, and limits +

Team history. Records use completed regular-season matchups, including scheduled games against the average team. All-play compares each real team’s score against every other real team’s score that week, with ties worth half a win. Expected wins sum those weekly win fractions. Schedule swing is recorded wins plus half of ties minus expected wins; it is a descriptive schedule measure, not proof of luck or managerial skill.

Scoring index. Each week’s points divided by that week’s real-team mean, multiplied by 100, then averaged over the team’s games. The all-time index is weighted by games played. Incomplete weekly fields produce unavailable comparison metrics rather than partial averages. The average placeholder is excluded from the comparison field from 2022 onward; team #12 was real before then.

Franchise identity. History follows ESPN team slots across renames and possible ownership changes. Season rows show that season’s team name and reported managers. A title is assigned to a franchise only when the historical record identifies its team slot. Pre-ESPN champions without matchup scores do not create game-level metrics. Head-to-head records cover the completed 2019–2025 regular-season and championship-bracket archive; consolation and placeholder games are excluded.

Trade scope. Executed trade packages are recovered from player-card transaction histories after scanning ESPN’s season player pool, including free agents and dropped players still in that pool. This is the recovered archive, not a guarantee that ESPN retained every transaction. The initial trade study covers 2025 and 2026; the importer can scan other available seasons. Current-year measurement excludes the active week, and trade-week points are always excluded.

Starter credit. Only actual, season-and-week-matched points in a recipient’s recorded starting slot and a scored matchup count. Bench, IR, and fantasy bye weeks contribute zero starter credit. Credit ends before an exit week or at the first missing roster appearance, and never restarts on reacquisition. Later flips, associated drops, roster-space costs, and replacement-level alternatives are outside this comparison. Postseason and consolation starts can count; player output runs through the league’s last measured scoring week regardless of ownership.

Missing data. A missing player stat is zero only when an unchanged NFL team’s documented bye explains it. Unknown points or lineups remain unavailable; incomplete starter coverage gets no starter-point edge. Before/after records are regular-season context, exclude the trade week, and have unequal sample sizes. They do not isolate the trade’s causal effect.
